tagline: The railroad and highway keep crossing one another.
intro: Route 70 turns out of the Sacramento Valley into the mountains and crosses the West Branch of the Feather River on a double-decker bridge, with the railroad on the lower deck. Past Jarbo Gap it drops into the canyon of the North Fork. Road and railroad mostly keep to opposite banks, and twice they cross the river and each other.

Three tunnels carry the road through the canyon rock. During construction, surveyors hung from ropes on steep granite slopes. Farther along, the route follows the East Branch toward Paxton before turning toward Quincy and the American Valley.

moments.title: Pulga Bridge
moments.text: The highway's arch spans the North Fork above a lower railroad truss bridge, so here the road rides over the tracks.

moments.title: Tobin Bridges
moments.text: The railroad crosses above Highway 70 as both routes bridge the North Fork, reversing the arrangement at Pulga.

moments.title: Paxton
moments.text: Once called Soda Bar and empty of residents at the 2020 census, Paxton sits just below the spot where Indian Creek and Spanish Creek join to form the East Branch.

sources.label: Wikipedia, East Branch North Fork Feather River
